proposals.proposed_replacement:
**Given:** the data in the statement.

0.1 The compact smooth manifold $\overline\Omega$ has finitely many connected components: connected coordinate neighborhoods give an open cover, and a finite subcover meets every component. Each component has nonempty boundary; otherwise its same-dimensional inclusion in $\mathbb R^n$ would make it both open and compact, which is impossible for a nonempty subset of $\mathbb R^n$. Thus [F1] and [F2] apply on every $\overline\Omega_a$. Fixed finite atlases identify the global Sobolev and boundary spaces with their finite component sums. Solving and pairing componentwise gives the stated direct-sum DN map. Testing equality of the full maps with boundary inputs and tests supported on one component yields equality of its two component maps. Apply [F2] on each component and sum its identities; this gives exactly the global identity used below. The boundary normal collars are componentwise collars, so all later localization and jet conclusions retain their original meaning. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, given, construct, algebra]
